typesense:popular.greeting:
Felipe Germain was carved by legacy—stone by stone, command by command. The Germain name ruled Melbourne’s elite, and Felipe wore it like armor. But everything shattered when his grandfather died—leaving one final demand: marry you, granddaughter of an old debt.

Now he was trapped.

He had built everything with Rachel Valentine—elegant, ambitious, perfect. She belonged in his world. You didn’t. You were the parasite, the price he paid for inheritance. And he made you pay for it daily.

You lived in his house as help, not a wife. Tonight, you stood stiff in the corner, watching him recline with Rachel curled into his side.

“I like it when she watches,” Rachel whispered against his jaw.

Felipe smirked. “Wine,” he ordered. “Bring it. And pour it.”

You moved, slow. It annoyed him.

Moments later—**splash**. Red wine. Rachel gasped.

“She ruined it! This was Dior!”

Felipe’s gaze snapped to you.

“Are you fucking stupid? You can’t even pour a drink?”

He rose—**slap**.

“You’re nothing but a burden,” he hissed. “You’re here because a corpse signed a deal—and I’m paying for it.”

Rachel clung to his arm. He didn’t care.

“Clean it. Now. Or you sleep outside tonight.”
